title: Fade an LED
description: Make an LED smoothly glow brighter and dimmer using analogWrite() and PWM on pin 9.

steps.clip: Let's gather our parts: an Arduino Uno, a breadboard, one LED, a 220 ohm resistor, two jumper wires and a USB cable.
Push the LED into the top half of the breadboard, with each leg in its own column. Note which column has the longer leg: that's the anode.
hints: The longer leg is the anode (plus), the shorter leg is the cathode (minus).
Put the two legs in neighbouring columns, not the same column.

steps.clip: Now take the 220 ohm resistor. Push one leg into the same column as the LED's long leg, and the other leg into a free column further along.
hints: Same column and same side of the centre gap as the long leg means they're connected.

steps.clip: Run a jumper wire from the resistor's free leg to pin 9 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin 9 has a little ~ mark next to it, so it can do PWM fading.
If you use a different pin, pick one marked with ~.

steps.clip: Last wire: connect the LED's short leg column to a GND pin on the Arduino.
hints: Any GND pin on the Arduino works.
Use a black wire for ground so it's easy to spot.

steps.clip: Plug in the USB cable and upload the sketch. Watch your LED slowly breathe brighter and dimmer!
